description: The Ork tutorial voiceover (autoloads/TutorialVoice.gd + tools/generate_tutorial_vo.py). Boots T1 from the real menu path and pins the player-facing behaviour: the narrator starts speaking the moment the first card appears and the clip it picks is the one belonging to THAT step; the card grows a 'Say It Again' button whose press restarts the same line; advancing a step swaps the clip; forcing controller mode re-renders the card through refresh_prompt() WITHOUT a step change and the spoken line must follow it from the kbm variant to the pad variant (this is the case the wiring exists for - a keyboard clip telling a Deck player to 'press I' is the bug); Settings > Audio > Tutorial Voiceover off cuts the line already in flight rather than letting it finish; and leaving the tutorial stops the narrator so an Ork is not explaining the charge phase over the main menu. Audio is silent under the harness (Dummy driver), so every assertion reads playback STATE (is_speaking / current_clip_id) rather than sound - the clips' audio content is validated offline by tools/generate_tutorial_vo.py.

steps.comment: the manifest loaded and carries the full lesson set
step 'welcome' on mouse+keyboard speaks the kbm variant of that step, not a stale or default clip
the voiceover's only on-screen affordance - without it nothing tells the player the card is narrated
a real click on the real button - replay after an explicit stop is the missed-the-instruction path
advancing a step swaps the line
the desktop policy LOCKS the mode, so a device claim is ignored by design - _force_mode is the policy's own entry point and is what a policy switch calls
THE case this wiring exists for: same step, different device, different words. A kbm clip here would tell a Deck player to press keys they do not have.
a player reaching for this switch is reacting to the voice talking RIGHT NOW - waiting for the clip to end reads as a broken toggle
leaving the tutorial has to take the voice with it
